title: Procurement micro-segmentation: SLA crediting & flexible insurance offsets for high-regulation partners
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Goal: Design and validate a procurement playbook + vendor-portal flow that lets account & partner teams offer targeted cost offsets (SLA credits and insurance premium subsidies) based on a vendor micro-segmentation model for regulated customers. The outcome should reduce enterprise procurement friction, preserve legal guardrails, and surface clear unit economics for subsidized onboarding.

Scope:
- Define micro-segmentation tiers (Trustlets) driven by evidence signals (SOC2 report, ephemeral attestation, isolation controls).
- Design a pricing experiment that offers a mix of SLA crediting (service credits for downtime/latency) and partial insurance premium offsets for vendors that cannot produce full SOC2 initially.
- Implement vendor-portal UI mocks and procurement playbook templates for AE/Solution Engineering to use in negotiation.
- Build contract amendment templates (legal + procurement) that enumerate subsidy duration, clawbacks, and evidence milestones.
- Instrument metrics and dashboards to evaluate adoption, procurement cycle time, and net unit economics.

Non-goals: Full legal negotiation of master agreements (this project produces templates and playbook only), and on-prem deployment automation (handled by Private product team).
acceptance_criteria: Micro-segmentation matrix (3 tiers) published with clear eligibility signals and evidence checklist
Pricing experiment design doc with at least 2 subsidy recipes (SLA crediting %, insurance offset %) and hypothesis statements
Vendor-portal mockups (login-to-acceptance flow) linked in Confluence and reviewed by Solutions Eng and Legal
Procurement playbook (one-pager) and 3 contract amendment templates uploaded to Drive
Dashboards: procurement cycle time, subsidy uptake rate, projected cost-to-Redwood, and early quality regressions instrumented
Pilot with 3 partner negotiations executed (recorded notes + feedback) and go/no-go recommendation documented
discussion: 2025-02-12 Priya Kapoor: Created ticket. Initial problem statement from AE team - several regulated customers are dropping deals due to absence of clear SOC2 path and unwillingness to pay full premium for 9-12 month SOC2 remediations.

2025-02-18 Diego Morales: Product kickoff with Solutions Eng / Legal. Agreed to pursue 3-tier micro-segmentation: Green (SOC2 present), Amber (SOC2 in progress + attestation), Grey (no SOC2 but compensating controls). Need legal input on clawback language.

2025-02-21 Legal (Ava Chen): Reviewed preliminary subsidy recipes. Redlines: require milestone-based evidence checkpoints and a sunset + clawback clause if evidence not delivered by X days. Will provide sample amendment language by 2025-02-28.
2025-02-25 Solutions Eng (Marta Ruiz): Shared 2 customer negotiation transcripts where partners accepted time-limited SLA credits in lieu of upfront SOC2 evidence. Logged as lessons for playbook.

2025-03-01 Diego Morales: Design review with UX. Uploaded first set of vendor-portal mocks to Confluence: /confluence/redwood/procurement/microsegmentation-mocks. Feedback: Add explicit cost-to-customer preview and clear expiry dates for subsidies.

2025-03-04 Priya Kapoor: Scheduled pilot cohort definition meeting (target 3 mid-market partners, prioritized by ARR and time-to-close). Need engineering dependency for portal acceptance endpoint (ENG-45802).

2025-03-05 Diego Morales: Updated acceptance criteria with dashboard metrics and pilot requirements. Draft of pricing experiment (A/B) published at /confluence/redwood/procurement/pricing-experiments/microsegmentation-v1
risks: Accounting: Subsidy needs clear recognition rules and an amortization approach (work with Finance).
Legal: Clawback language may slow negotiations or be rejected by some partners; need fallback conservative template.
Operational: Manual review required for Amber/Grey tiers initially; if volume grows, we must automate attestation ingestion or hire vendor-triage team.
Economic: If uptake exceeds projections, Redwood bears insurance-premium-like cost profile — cap required in playbook.
Security: Grey-tier allowances cannot bypass critical controls (network isolation, segregation of PII).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (2 weeks): Finalize micro-segmentation matrix and legal amendment templates.
Phase 1 (4 weeks): Implement vendor-portal acceptance UI and add 'subsidy offer' card in AE toolbelt (internal only).
Phase 2 (8 weeks): Run A/B pricing experiment across 3 pilot negotiations; collect qualitative feedback and usage metrics.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Analyze results, update playbook, and recommend scaled launch or iterate on subsidy recipes.
metrics: Procurement cycle time (days) — baseline vs pilot
Subsidy uptake rate (%) — % of eligible negotiations that accept the subsidy
Net unit economics per pilot (projected cost to Redwood vs incremental ARR closed)
Compliance attainment rate — % of pilots that reach required evidence milestones within defined windows
Legal review turnaround time (days) for amendment acceptance
